read_this_first: THE CLAIM, IN THE CODING DOMAIN: let the system experience a fix once and it has learned it, so the next bug is repaired from what was learned. MEASURED with the tree's own organ for exactly that, NOT EDITED: VerifiedSkillStore (canonical/swe_kernel/verified_skill_crystallizer_v1.py) -- crystallize_code_fix takes one verified fix and stores a rule, recall_and_apply_verified proposes a patch for new source from the stored rules and accepts it only if the target's tests pass -- with its own test oracle (ProjectTestOracle), called the way the tree's production repair session calls them. THE BUGS: QuixBugs (github.com/jkoppel/QuixBugs), 40 small Python programs with a defect on one line each, their own tests and their published correct versions; nobody here wrote any of it, and it is the easiest setting program repair has. Checked first: all 40 buggy versions fail their tests and all 40 pass with the published fix applied. RESULT. (1) Of the 40 fixes the organ STORED 22 AS LESSONS AND REFUSED 18: 14 because the rule it formed did not pass the organ's own check on a mutated twin of the program, 3 because the buggy program does not finish within the 8 seconds its tests are given, so no failing test could be counted, 1 as not generalisable. (2) THE SAME BUG AGAIN, on a fresh copy: 22 of 22 repaired from memory. That part is real. (3) ONE FIX, THEN ANOTHER BUG: 22 lessons times the 39 other bugs is 858 pairs. With the organ's production defaults 1 pair is repaired; with every generalisation it offers switched on, 3. In the widest setting 19 of the 22 lessons repair no other bug, and no lesson repairs more than one. (4) ALL THE OTHER FIXES, THEN THIS BUG (21 or 22 lessons held at once): 1 of 40 with the defaults, 3 of 40 with everything on. (5) WHAT THE TREE SHIPS WITH as already learned (the 2 Python rules of its seed bundle), nothing taught here: 0 of 40. The transfers are listed under repairs_of_another_bug with the patch: two are a comparison made inclusive (< to <=, > to >=) carried to another comparison, one is two names exchanged; all three pass the target's tests, one is the published fix and two are other correct-looking fixes. So a lesson reaches another bug when the other bug is the same small change, and otherwise not. FOR SCALE, as reported in the papers listed under published_results_on_the_same_bugs and not reproduced here: language models repair 31 to 40 of these same 40 bugs with no lesson at all. Nothing here searches for a fix; the tree's repair solver, which does, was not run in this measurement (see not_done), so this says what a lesson adds, not what the tree can repair. Every recall got a store of its own holding only the lessons meant for it; in 'all the other fixes' the bug's own lesson is never among them (tested). No model is called anywhere. Producer-run in a sandbox; nobody else has repeated it.
